task_description: Grouped matmul: 8 row-blocks of a (128, 64) input, each multiplied by one of 4 (64, 64) expert weight matrices per a per-block group_id array -- the core shape of MoE routing (JAXBench's 10p_Sparse_MoE, 11p_Megablox_GMM, 14p_Ragged_Dot) and paged-attention page-table gathers (6p/7p).

metrics.name: vmem_resident_weight_elems
metrics.description: number of weight-tensor elements resident in VMEM per grid step. Naive: G*K*N (all experts, every step). Optimized: K*N (only the routed expert, via scalar-prefetch-driven index_map). Exact and verifiable from the code/config alone -- this is what the technique actually buys, and it scales with G even though this cell uses a small G=4 to keep the example fast to verify.

metrics.name: achieved_tflops_pct_of_peak_bf16
metrics.description: secondary/confirmatory signal, same convention as other cells. At this cell's small scale the VMEM-footprint story is the more direct one; the throughput gap should widen with larger G.

note: Row added after reading all 50 JAXBench workloads (not one of Hawkeye's original 10 GPU rows) -- see taxonomy/README.md's 'Row provenance' section for why. optimized_kernel.py uses pltpu.PrefetchScalarGridSpec; its exact calling convention (scalar-prefetch ref first in both the kernel body and each BlockSpec's index_map) was verified by direct experimentation against this jax/jaxlib version, not copied from an official example -- the convention worked on the first attempt but has not been cross-checked against Pallas's own documentation.
